bib.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

read.skipped: References skimmed. Supplementary material (training and inference parameters, ablation details) is referenced but not in the PDF.

question: How can spatial conditions (edges, depth, pose, segmentation) be added to a large pretrained text-to-image diffusion model without destroying it, even with small condition datasets?
hypothesis: Locking the pretrained model, training a copy of its encoder, and joining them with zero-initialized convolutions gives robust learning of conditions without harmful noise or forgetting.
contributions: ControlNet architecture adding spatially localized input conditions to a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model via efficient finetuning
Pretrained ControlNets for Stable Diffusion on Canny edges, Hough lines, scribbles, human key points, segmentation, normals, depth, cartoon line drawings
Ablations against alternative architectures and user studies against baselines

method.summary: A trainable copy of Stable Diffusion's 12 encoder blocks and middle block receives a condition (encoded by a small 4-conv network) and feeds back into the locked U-Net through zero-initialized 1x1 convolutions. Trained with the standard noise-prediction loss, with 50% of prompts blanked.

datasets.name: Condition datasets (edge, depth, pose, segmentation etc.)
datasets.size: 1k, 50k and 3m images in the dataset-size study (Fig 10); abstract: small (<50k) and large (>1m)
datasets.preprocessing: Conditions extracted with Canny, MiDaS-style depth (Ranftl), normal map, M-LSD, HED, ADE20K, Openpose, sketches; details in unseen supplement

datasets.name: Depth training set for SDv2 ControlNet

models.name: Stable Diffusion V1.5 / V2.1 + ControlNet
models.architecture: Latent-diffusion U-Net: 12 encoder blocks, 1 middle, 12 decoder blocks (25 total; 8 up/down-sampling, 17 main blocks each with 4 resnet layers and 2 ViTs); CLIP text encoder; 64x64 latents from 512x512 images
models.init_from: Stable Diffusion (locked); ControlNet copy initialised from SD encoder weights; zero convs from zero; condition encoder E from Gaussian
models.layers: 25 blocks in SD; ControlNet copies 12 encoder + 1 middle

other.condition_encoder: 4 conv layers, 4x4 kernels, stride 2, ReLU, 16/32/64/128 channels
other.overhead: about 23% more GPU memory and 34% more time per iteration on one A100 PCIE 40GB

models.name: ControlNet-lite
models.architecture: Each block's trainable copy replaced with a single convolution layer

models.name: ControlNet without zero convolutions
models.architecture: Zero convs replaced by Gaussian-initialised standard convs

other.training: large NVIDIA A100 cluster, thousands of GPU hours, more than 12M images

models.name: OneFormer
models.architecture: segmentation model used to re-detect segments in generated images

training.objective: L = E[ ||eps - eps_theta(z_t, t, c_t, c_f)||_2^2 ] (noise prediction); 50% of text prompts replaced with empty strings
training.steps: 'usually in less than 10K optimization steps' to sudden convergence; Fig 4 shows steps 100 to 12000 (convergence at 6133 in the example)
training.regularisation: Original SD weights locked; zero convolutions
training.hardware: Depth ControlNet for SDv2: single NVIDIA RTX 3090Ti; overhead test on one A100 PCIE 40GB

other.note: The paper defers detailed training parameters to the supplementary material, which is not in the PDF

inference.samples: Ablation: random batch of 6 samples per setting, no cherry-picking; SDv2-D2I comparison: 200 images; user study: 20 sketches x 5 methods
inference.prompting: Default prompt 'a high-quality, detailed, and professional image'; four ablation prompt settings: none, insufficient, conflicting, perfect

parameters.cfg_resolution_weighting: Add condition to eps_c only, then weight each SD-ControlNet connection w_i = 64/h_i with h_1=8, h_2=16, ..., h_13=64
parameters.multi_condition: Outputs of multiple ControlNets added directly, no extra weighting

metrics.name: Average User Ranking (AUR; also called AHR in text)
metrics.definition: Users rank 5 methods 1 to 5 (worst to best) on result quality and condition fidelity

metrics.name: IoU
metrics.definition: OneFormer re-segments generated images; IoU against ADE20K ground-truth labels

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance over randomly generated 512x512 sets

metrics.name: User precision in telling SDv2-D2I from ControlNet
metrics.definition: 12 users shown 100 images from each to learn, then tell which model made each of 200 images

eval.protocol: 12 users ranked 20 groups of 5 results, giving 100 rankings for quality and 100 for fidelity; single run, no significance test stated; ± values appear to be spread but are not defined

results.quote: The average precision of the users is 0.52 ± 0.17, indicating that the two method yields almost indistinguishable results.

limits: Detailed training and inference hyperparameters (optimizer, learning rate, batch size) are only in supplementary material, absent from the PDF.
User studies are small (12 users, 20 sketches) and ± values are undefined.
Ablation is qualitative (6 uncherry-picked samples per setting) with no metric.
PITI uses a different backbone (GLIDE), so comparison is not like for like (authors' note).
Quantitative comparison only covers segmentation and sketch; depth comparison is a user discrimination test only.
